Beginner Guide: How This Call Trade Works in Plain Dollars

Why this spread works differently from buying shares: Selling the upper $198 call collects $18.86/sh upfront, lowering your breakeven to $178.96 and protecting you against post-news volatility crush.

Exact wallet math (1 contract = 100 shares): You buy the $178.91 Call for $14.60 and simultaneously sell the $198 Call for $18.86, paying $0.05/sh net ($600.00 total for 120 spread(s)). That $600.00 is the absolute maximum you can lose.

Breakeven & profit ceiling: At expiry (2027-01-15), you start making money above $178.96 (-1.4% from $181.54). Anywhere at or above $198, your $600.00 turns into $229,080.00 (+$228,480.00 net profit).

Speed & time decay in plain English: Today, each $1 move up in FAS adds ~$6,984.00 to your spread (Net Delta), while sitting flat costs ~$1,502.40/day in time decay (Net Theta) — much lower than an unhedged call because the sold $198 call decays in your favor.
